subject: On-call retainer + matchback credits — pricing and coverage details
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@acme-analytics.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Redwood Sales <sales@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify on on-call retainer + matchback credits for SLA

Hi Logan,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team liked the routing/fallback logic. Procurement asked me to get clarity on two things before we move to legal: 1) how the on-call retainer works alongside your uptime SLO credits (we call them matchbacks internally), and 2) whether you can provide a blended monthly price if we commit to annual spend across Hosted + Dedicated.

Concretely:
- We need 24/7 escalation for P1s and a named escalation engineer for critical incidents.
- Our procurement team wants a clear mechanism for credits if you miss the 99.95% uptime window. Do credits apply to compute spend only, to the retainer, or both?
- Any volume/commit discounts for a 12-month committed spend (targeting $500k ARR)?

Can you send a short proposal with exact response windows, how matchback calculations will be applied, and an indicative price? Legal will need an attachment they can use for PO routing.

Thanks,
Elena
Director, Procurement
Acme Analytics

---
Elena Morales
Acme Analytics
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0182
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj@acme-analytics.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 10:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify on on-call retainer + matchback credits for SLA

Hi Elena — appreciate the concise list. Attached is a short proposal (oncall_retainer_proposal_v1.pdf) that outlines 3 retainer tiers, how matchbacks are calculated, and a starter pricing slice for Hosted + Dedicated. Key points up front: 

- Coverage: 24/7 P1 on-call with 60-minute initial response, P2 same-business-day response (4 hours), P3 next-business-day. Named escalation engineer assigned for P1s.
- Matchback model: credits are applied to monthly service invoice. Credits are calculated as a percentage of the impacted service charges for the affected region (compute + platform fee). The retainer itself is not automatically credited — instead we amortize credits against service spend, which is how our finance team prefers to book it.
- Pricing: base retainer tiers are $8k/mo (bronze), $18k/mo (silver), $32k/mo (gold) for 24/7 coverage. For annual committed spend >= $500k, we can offer a blended discount on retainer (10%) and a separate committed discount on usage (tiered; see attachment).

I've put a couple of optional items in the attachment: weekend-only on-call (reduced retainer) and an escalation retainer that guarantees a named engineer within 30 minutes for an additional $6k/mo.

Next steps: if this looks directionally correct, Aditya can propose a committed spend discount structure and Camila (CS) will add the detailed escalation runbook to the SOW. I also included a DocuSign placeholder link in the proposal for faster routing.

Best,
Logan
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachment: oncall_retainer_proposal_v1.pdf (1 page — pricing table + coverage matrix)
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@acme-analytics.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:31:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify on on-call retainer + matchback credits for SLA

Hi Elena — adding the CS perspective so you have the operational specifics for legal/SRE review.

Operational details (summary):
- Escalation tiers: Tier 1 (on-call engineer) — initial ack in 60 mins; Tier 2 (on-call senior) — within 2 hours; Tier 3 (named escalation engineer) — within 4 hours unless escalation retainer purchased (then 30 mins).
- Coverage matrix: 24/7 includes holidays. Weekend-only retainer covers Saturday/Sunday 08:00–20:00 PT.
- Matchback calculation: downtime window is measured against model-serving endpoints in the affected region; we calculate average impacted token throughput and apply credit as percentage of the monthly service fees for those endpoints. Example in the proposal shows a 0.5% credit for 99.9–99.95, 1.5% for 99.5–99.9, and higher tiers above that.
- Runbooks & access: we will provide a read-only incident dashboard link and a shared PagerDuty rotation.

I can convert this into a short SOW paragraph (for the SOW addendum) — ping me with any edits and I'll sync with legal to make it redline-friendly.

— Camila
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@acme-analytics.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 12:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify on on-call retainer + matchback credits for SLA

Elena — quick commercial note from my side. If Acme is comfortable with a 12-month committed spend of $500k+ (Hosted + Dedicated combined), Redwood can: 

- Apply a 12% discount to the standard retainer price (applies to whichever retainer tier you choose)
- Offer an additional $25k of onboarding credits that can be used for Professional Services or to offset first-month usage charges
- Include a capped Service Credit Guarantee: if monthly uptime < 99.9% we provide a credit equal to 5% of that month’s impacted regional fees (to be tracked via the incident report and verified by our SRE team).

This is conditional on a 12-month payment term and an SOW that specifies the endpoints and regions in scope. I'm linking the HubSpot deal for clarity: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345 — open to a short call this week to lock numbers and hand to legal.

— Aditya
Senior Account Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Elena Morales <elena@acme-analytics.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj@acme-analytics.com>, procurement@acme-analytics.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 15:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify on on-call retainer + matchback credits for SLA

Thanks — this is helpful and aligns with what procurement needs. A couple quick points: 
- Acme is comfortable proceeding on a 12-month commit in the $500k range if you can convert the onboarding credit into an offset against month 1 usage rather than PS-only.
- Please include the capped Service Credit Guarantee language in the SOW addendum and put the escalation retainer as an optional line item.

Procurement has attached our PO template (acme_po_template.pdf) and asked that you provide a final SOW and DocuSign link so they can execute quickly. If you can send a redline-ready SOW by end of day Wed (18 Nov), procurement can route internally and get this into legal.

Acceptance in principle — please send the final doc and I will route for signature.

Best,
Elena
Director, Procurement
Acme Analytics

Attachment: acme_po_template.pdf
